run.question: List the top 5 largest Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' by document count. Show their names and doc counts.

report.summary: Listing Elasticsearch indices matching 'app-184-*' matched 1800 indices; the full view exceeded the size limit, so the backend's docs.count-descending ordering was read back as a 10-row slice starting at row 0. The five largest are an exact five-way tie at 500 documents: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25, app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10, app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20, app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15, each health=green status=open with store.size between 46.7kb and 47.9kb. Immediately after them in the same ordering the shown rows drop to docs.count 1 (store.size 7.5kb), so nothing shown exceeds 500 documents. The order among the five tied indices is the backend's tie order, not a ranking. Counts are point-in-time at the query (observed_at 2026-11-23T17:23:33Z); the indices listing has no time range, so it cannot show counts during the incident window. No health or causal conclusion is drawn from these counts.

claims.text: The 'app-184-*' index listing matched 1800 indices in total (total_rows 1800; the adopted read slice returned rows 0-9 of that ordering and reported 1790 omitted rows).

The five largest indices matching 'app-184-*' by docs.count, all tied at 500 documents and all health=green status=open: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (500 docs, 47.8kb), app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (500 docs, 46.9kb), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (500 docs, 47.9kb), app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (500 docs, 46.8kb), app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (500 docs, 46.7kb).

Immediately after the five 500-document indices in the same docs.count:desc ordering, the shown rows drop to docs.count 1 (app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.09, app-184-data-db-2024.01.34, app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.08, app-184-data-db-2024.01.35, app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.07, each 7.5kb), which places the five 500-document indices at the top of the ordering for the rows shown.

The document counts are point-in-time readings at the query (observed_at 2026-11-23T17:23:33Z through 17:23:41Z); evidence notes state that this index listing has no time range at the source, so it cannot show document counts as they were earlier in the authorized window.

Because the top four indices are dated 2024.01.05-2024.01.20 and five separate indices carry an identical 500-document count, these may be fixed-size seed/test indices rather than live data volumes; this is unverified, as no document contents or write-activity counters were examined.

For a tie-free ranking and full coverage of all 1800 matches, query _cat/indices or per-index stats with an explicit numeric sort, and narrow the pattern (for example app-184-ml-* or app-184-data-*) so results fit the view limit instead of relying on a sliced 1800-row listing.

gaps: The read slice was truncated: only rows 0-9 of 1800 were shown (1790 rows omitted), so rows 10-1799 were not inspected; the claim that no index exceeds 500 documents rests on the docs.count-descending ordering of the slice actually read, not on the unread rows.
The relative ordering among the five indices tied at 500 documents is the backend's tie order and does not rank them against each other.
Two attempts to sort the listing client-side via jq failed with JQ_RUNTIME_ERROR, so the ranking could not be recomputed over all 1800 rows; the first oversized listing view was not citable.
Document counts are as of the query at 2026-11-23T17:23:32-41Z only; no sample describes the state of these indices earlier in the authorized window.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so when these indices were created or last modified is unknown.
next_steps: If per-index creation time or write activity is needed, check _cat/indices with creation.date columns or per-index index_stats counters (cumulative, not window-scoped).
If a tie-free top-N is required, obtain numbering from _cat/indices sorted numerically on docs.count rather than the default listing order.
